---
title: "OLS verification in R, statsmodels and PHP"
---

phit's `fit_ols_matrix()` is compared with R's `lm()` and statsmodels' `OLS` on the same observations. The [verification notebook](../notebooks/ols-verification.qmd) shows the calls and results side by side, and the [math notebook](../notebooks/ols-math.qmd) derives the calculations. Shared metrics and tolerance conventions are described in [Verification](../verification.qmd).

## Compared

Coefficients, covariance, standard errors, t statistics, p-values, 95% confidence intervals, fitted values, residuals, R-squared, and log-likelihood. The models use an intercept, homoskedastic covariance, residual variance RSS/(n − p), Student's t tests, and ML variance RSS/n for the likelihood.

## Inputs and scope

| Case | Input / retained n | Model |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Simulated housing | 8 / 8 | Intercept and floor area |
| Simulated housing, multiple | 8 / 8 | Intercept, area and correlated bedrooms |
| Simple | 5 / 5 | Intercept and one predictor |
| Multiple | 10 / 10 | Intercept and two predictors |
| No intercept | 10 / 10 | Two predictors, uncentered R-squared |
| Correlated | 10 / 10 | Intercept and two correlated full-rank predictors |
| Listwise missing | 6 / 4 | One predictor-null row and one outcome-null row omitted |

The housing rows in `docs/data/housing.csv` are simulated; the [math notebook](../notebooks/ols-math.qmd) describes how they were generated. The other cases come from `tests/fixtures/ols-r.json`.

## Reference and versions

R 4.6.1 `lm()`, statsmodels 0.15.0 with NumPy 2.5.4 on Python 3.14, and phit on PHP 8.5.10, all on the development Mac. Linux and other PHP builds are not covered by this report.

```r
observations <- read.csv("docs/data/housing.csv")
fit <- lm(monthly_rent ~ area_m2, data = observations, na.action = na.omit)
summary(fit)
confint(fit, level = 0.95)
logLik(fit)
```

```python
observations = pd.read_csv("docs/data/housing.csv")
X = sm.add_constant(observations[["area_m2"]])
fit = sm.OLS(observations["monthly_rent"], X, missing="drop", hasconst=True).fit(use_t=True)
```

```php
// Each row of $x is [1.0, area_m2]; $y holds monthly_rent.
$result = Phit\fit_ols_matrix(
    x: $x,
    y: $y,
    intercept: false,
);
```

The runner gives every implementation the same explicit design. R receives it as `y ~ . - 1` and computes R-squared with the same ones-column convention as phit, which avoids a duplicate intercept.

## Metric and tolerance

Every field, relative to R: absolute 1e-9 plus relative 1e-7.

## Results

All fields in all seven cases pass. [ols-results.json](ols-results.json) holds the inputs, versions, sample metadata, PHP warnings, and differences from R.

In the missing-data case, positions 1 and 3 are dropped and 0, 2, 4, and 5 are retained. phit emits one `E_WARNING` with the dropped and original counts. The runner checks the positions and counts and records the warning.

## Known exceptions

- Perfect and zero fits, and invalid or singular inputs, are covered by the Rust and PHP tests, not this comparison. Tiny decomposition-dependent residuals make perfect-fit t, p, and likelihood comparisons unstable.
- R and statsmodels may accept a singular design by aliasing coefficients. phit rejects it.

## Reproduction

After the [notebook setup](../notebooks/index.qmd):

```sh
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_ols.py
```

The script refits every case with Rscript, statsmodels, and PHP, checks every field, and rewrites `ols-results.json`. `cargo test` and `tests/ols.php` run without R or Python.

Sources: [R lm](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/stats/html/lm.html), [statsmodels OLS](https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/generated/statsmodels.regression.linear_model.OLS.html), [statsmodels missing data](https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/missing.html).
